newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher but off earlier highs.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher but off earlier highs.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher but off their intraday highs on a mixture of late profit taking and pressure from country-related hedging, traders said.
"We're seeing some wheat moving in the country so hedging's coming in," a KCBT trader said at the close.
"Profit taking late allowed our market to retrace its over-extended gains," another trader said. "This could set us up for further weakness tomorrow morning."
Traders said Benson-Quinn, which had been an early buyer of at least two million March bushels, had turned seller late.

KCBT wheat was boosted at the midsession on technical fund-buying, which followed early gains caused by nervousness over the extent of rain-related damage to Argentina's wheat crop and by concern over possible cold damage to U.S. wheat.
Nearby KCBT Dec was firm on ideas that the delivered wheat being stopped by E D & F Man International will be loaded out of Kansas City, thereby reducing deliverable stocks.

KCBT wheat closed two to 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up 9-1/2 cents at $4.63-1/2. March gained 4-1/4 cents to close at $4.15-1/4. Earlier, March had set an intraday high at $4.25, its highest intraday level since Oct. 15, 1996.

FIMAT and Benson-Quinn were early buyers of the March, picking up at least 5.3 million bushels combined. Rosenthal Collins, E D & F Man International and ADM's Smoot Grain bought a combined 6.8 million March. Prudential and CIS each sold at least two million March.
